working_title: How London Survived its Greatest Inferno
hook: Could a single bakery spark a firestorm that swallowed an entire medieval city?

scenes.narration: In September 1666, London was a crowded maze of wooden houses.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of narrow medieval timber houses with overhanging upper floors nearly touching across a cobbled London alley, warm ochre and teal palette, visible paper grain, soft rim light, gentle depth haze, calm composition, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: It began past midnight on Pudding Lane as embers caught fuel.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of a cozy dark bakery interior with glowing orange embers on a stone hearth, warm brick red and ochre tones, visible paper grain, soft rim light, calm composition, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: At dawn, strong east winds fanned sparks into a wall of flames.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of thick orange and amber flames rising against a smoky morning sky above timber rooftops, warm muted palette, visible paper grain, gentle depth haze, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: Historians note the Lord Mayor hesitated, fearing property costs.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of a worried official in a wide-brimmed hat gesturing before medieval wooden facades, deep brick red and teal palette, visible paper grain, soft rim light, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: By Monday, panic gripped the streets as families fled.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of townspeople with bundles and carts crowding toward a heavy stone medieval city gate, warm ochre tones, visible paper grain, soft rim light, gentle depth haze, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: On Tuesday, the fire consumed Old Saint Paul's Cathedral.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of a grand Gothic cathedral silhouette partially framed by gentle smoke and warm amber glow, muted teal and brick red palette, visible paper grain, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: On Wednesday, winds died and the garrison used gunpowder.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of the stone Tower of London under a clearing smoky sky with calm light, warm ochre and teal palette, visible paper grain, soft rim light, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: Though devastated, London rose again on its historic street plan.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of a new brick and stone street curving between rebuilding homes under a warm morning sun, ochre and brick red palette, visible paper grain, vertical 9:16 framing.

scenes.narration: From catastrophe came a reimagined capital. Subscribe to explore history.
scenes.visual: Hand-painted gouache storybook illustration of the fluted Portland stone Monument standing tall near the Thames, warm muted palette of ochre and teal, visible paper grain, soft rim light, gentle depth haze, vertical 9:16 framing.

call_to_action: Subscribe to explore more hidden stories from history.
why_it_matters: Understanding the Great Fire of London reveals how a devastating urban disaster reshaped architectural resilience and community survival in the seventeenth century.
structure: Countdown of the key moments that led to the outcome, building tension toward the final one.

claims.claim: In September 1666, London was a crowded maze of wooden houses.
It began past midnight on Pudding Lane as embers caught fuel.
At dawn, strong east winds fanned sparks into a wall of flames.
Historians note the Lord Mayor hesitated, fearing property costs.
claims.note: Lord Mayor Sir Thomas Bloodworth hesitated because most premises were rented and owners could not be found.
